# Home page

`/` stops redirecting to Scores and becomes a home page for the current season.

**Approved mockup:** round 5 (`.superpowers/brainstorm/34473-1792609983/content/home-v5g.html`, generated by the session scratchpad's `v5gen.py`). It was built on real week 7 data from 2026.

**Sections, top to bottom:**
- the **top row**: this week's game of the week as a banner, with two tagged games beside it
- **standings** (all teams), with a **results** card and a **top performers** card in a rail on the right
- **league leaders** in a gold band

The scores ticker and the nav stay above it as on every page. The full Standings page stays as it is. "Full table" links to it.

## Which weeks

- **This week** is the ticker's week: `tickerWeek(season, liveWeekNumber(...))`. That is the live week while games are on, otherwise the first unplayed week.
- **The results week** is the last played week, `season.lastScoredWeek`.
- Labels always use the week number, never "last week". The results card is titled "Week 6", and top performers is "Week 6 · Top performers".

Both switch on the Tuesday sync: once week 7 is marked played, the results cards show week 7 and the top row moves to week 8.

## Top row

**Layout:**
- The banner takes the left column and the two tagged games stack in a 270 px column on the right.
- The banner stretches to the height of that column.
- Under 900 px, the side games drop below the banner, side by side, and then stack at phone width.

**The banner:**
- Each team's photo sits at the outer edge, cut diagonally, with a 5 px stripe along the cut: sky on the left, coral on the right.
- A team with no avatar gets its manager's initials on the panel.
- Each side shows:
  - the team name, a link to `/teams/{year}/{userId}`
  - below it, the manager name, record and rank
- In the middle:
  - a large "Game of the week" title
  - the state label and the two scores
  - the win % bar
- The whole banner links to the box score, except where a team name link is clicked.

**The two tagged games:**
- Each card shows the tag, the state label, and then one row per team: avatar, team name (linked), record and score.
- The card links to the box score.

### Three states

The state comes from `gameOutlook` (`upcoming` / `live` / `final`), the same as the ticker.

| | Label | Scores | Under the scores |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Before kickoff** | "Projected" | projected totals, both in the same neutral colour | win % bar from the projections |
| **Live** | red dot with "Live", plus the ESPN clock of the latest game for those rosters, e.g. "Sun 3:12 PM" | current points, both neutral | each side's projected final and players left to play; live win % bar |
| **Final** | "Final" | winner bright and bold, loser dimmed | "{winner team} by {margin}" |

- Side games follow the same three states, with the label on the right of the tag.
- Neither side is highlighted until the game is final.

### Choosing the games

The choice is worked out from the synced projections only, so it doesn't change during the week as live points come in.

**Game of the week, regular season.** Each game gets a score of `closeness × stakes²`:
- `closeness = 1 − 2·|p − 0.5|`, where `p` is the pre-game win probability from `gameOutlook` with nothing played yet
- `stakes` is the average of `(N + 1 − rank) / N` for both teams, using current standings with N teams

Squaring stakes favours games between good teams over a coin flip between two bad ones. Ties go to the higher combined projection, then the lower matchup id. In week 7 this picks J's vs The Window.

**Tags, regular season.** Two side slots, filled in this order of priority. A game can hold only one slot and is never the game of the week. Each tag fills at most one slot, and a tag with no qualifying game is skipped.

1. **Upset alert:** the projected favourite has fewer wins than the underdog. Of the games that qualify, take the one with the biggest gap in wins.
2. **Champ on upset watch:** last season's champion (`honors.champion` of the previous season) is projected to lose. The champion's team gets 🏆 after its name.
3. **Top of the table:** the game with the #1 team.
4. **Shootout:** the highest combined projection.

**Playoff weeks:**
- The banner is the championship game in the final week, and the highest-seeded winners-bracket game before that.
- The side slots are the next winners-bracket games, labelled with their bracket tag via `fmtTag`.
- The tag colours keep their meaning: coral for upset alert, turf for the champion, sky for everything else.

**Season complete:** the banner shows the championship final and the side slots show the third-place game and the toilet bowl. Any game that doesn't exist is left out.

**Before week 1 has games:** the top row is hidden.

## Standings

- Every team, using the same columns and look as the Standings page: rank, team (photo, linked team name, manager underneath), W, L, PF, PA and streak.
- A "Playoff cut" divider sits after `playoffTeams`.
- The top two ranks get the highlighted rank chip.
- The header says "Regular season · Standings" and has a "Full table" link to `/standings/{year}`.
- The table reuses `StandingsTable` with a compact prop if the existing markup fits; otherwise it's a new `HomeStandings` that takes the same rows.
- It reflects the synced standings only. It doesn't change during a live game.

## Rail

**Results card**, titled "Week N", with "Results" above it and a link to the Scores page for that week. Three quick hitters, each with the manager's photo:

| Hitter | Rule | Text | Number |
|---|---|---|---|
| High score | the highest team score that week | manager, with the team name muted | the score |
| Blowout | the largest margin | "{winner manager} over {loser manager}" | +margin |
| Nail-biter | the smallest margin | "{winner manager} over {loser manager}" | +margin |

Ties go to the lower matchup id.

**Top performers card**, titled "Week N · Top performers", with a link to `/stats/players`:
- The five highest-scoring starters that week, in league scoring. Ties go to the player name.
- Each row has:
  - a headshot
  - first line: the player name, linked to `/player/{id}`, with the position
  - second line: the manager who started them
  - third line, muted: the full stat line, for example "16 car, 64 yds, 2 TD · 9/10 rec, 53 yds · 1 fum"
  - the points, in plain ink
- A stat line builder covers passing (cmp/att, yds, TD, INT), rushing (car, yds, TD), receiving (rec/tgt, yds, TD) and fumbles lost. Parts that are zero are left out.

## League leaders

The `leaders` sub-tab moves off Records and onto the home page, in a full-width band with a gold tint.

**Header:** "League leaders", with "{year} · through week N" above it, and a position filter (All / QB / RB / WR / TE) on the right.

**Three category columns:** Most points, Most yards and Most touchdowns.
- Each column has a spotlight card for #1: a large headshot, the value, and the team and manager.
- Under it are ranks 2–5, each with a headshot, a linked name and a bar scaled to #1.
- Most yards and Most touchdowns each have a small All / Pass / Rush / Rec switch. These switches cover the six board variants that are leaving Records.

**Right-hand panel:** "Beating the model": the top 5 by FPOE, with a switch to xFP.

**Dropped:** Most touches is not carried over. It's the only leaders board that isn't kept.

**Data:**
- Everything comes from the existing leader board functions (`leadPoints`, `leadYards`, `leadTouchdowns`, `leadRushYards`, …, `leadFpoe`, `leadXfp`), fed by `flattenLines(seasons, players)` for the current year, with `fitXfp` on all lines.
- These are the same numbers Records showed, in one points source (league scoring).
- Player names link to `/player/{id}`.

**Gold applies to:** eyebrow labels, the spotlight card wash and value, the bars, and the active filter chip. The band background is a dark warm gradient in dark mode and a pale gold wash in light mode.

**Records:**
- Remove `leaders` from `SUB_TABS`, along with the "Season has not started" special case in `RecordsView`.
- `?sub=leaders` falls back to the first sub-tab, as an unknown sub already does.

## Live

The home page reads `useLive()` and calls `weekStatus` (moved from `ScoreTicker` to `lib/live/weekStatus.ts`). There is no new fetching.

- Live points, the clock and the outlook are already polled every 60 seconds by `LiveProvider` while a game is on.
- The home page doesn't call `useLiveStats`. Stat lines are only needed for box scores.
- Results, top performers, standings and leaders use synced data only.

## Routing and data

- **Index route:** `/` renders `HomePage`. Its loader is `loadAllSeasons()`, the same as Records, because the leaders and FPOE fit need every season's lines. The home page takes the current season from that list.
- **Scores:** `/scores` keeps its redirect.
- **Nav:** the brand link already points to `/`.

**New modules:**
- `lib/home/pick.ts`: game of the week and tags (`pickGames(season, week, prevSeason) → { hero: Game | null, sides: { game: Game; tag: SideTag }[] }`)
- `lib/home/results.ts`: quick hitters and top performers (`weekHitters(week)`, `topPerformers(week, n)`, `statLine(stats)`)
- `lib/live/weekStatus.ts`: moved from `ScoreTicker`
- **Components:** `components/home/`
  - `GameBanner`
  - `SideGame`
  - `HomeStandings` (if it's needed)
  - `ResultsCard`
  - `TopPerformers`
  - `LeadersBand` with `LeaderColumn` and `ModelPanel`

## Theme

- Built on the app's existing colour tokens, and works in both light and dark mode.
- The mockup's dark palette becomes the dark-mode values. Light mode keeps the same structure on light surfaces.
- The sky and coral team colours, the turf "good" colour and the gold leaders colour are added as tokens if they're missing.
- Headings use the condensed display face from the mockup (Barlow Condensed) if the app already loads it. Otherwise it's added for the home page headings only.

## Testing

**`pick.ts`:**
- week 7 2026 picks J's vs The Window as the game of the week, with Upset alert (adildo vs faraz525) and Champ on upset watch (Shivi1 vs mattygggg) beside it
- tie-breaking
- a tag with no qualifying game is skipped
- playoff weeks and a completed season
- a week with fewer than three games

**`results.ts`:**
- each hitter's rule and tie-breaks
- top five ordering
- stat line formatting, including zero parts left out

**`HomePage`:**
- renders the three states from a stubbed `useLive`
- the winner is highlighted only when final
- the links go to the team, player, box score, standings and scores pages
- the top row is hidden before week 1

**Records:** has no Leaders sub-tab.

**`ScoreTicker`:** its tests still pass after `weekStatus` moves.
